content:
We got two templates. Need to find which when applied to the given molecule reproduces the reaction (retro step). The task: return mapped_rxn and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The template_id likely is reaction_id? In result entries, there is 'reaction_id' field. Probably template_id is that integer. Need to test each template on the molecule to see if applying yields precursors that match description? The reaction is carbonyl-ene intramolecular forming five-membered ring with hydroxyl. The given molecule: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1... )... It has a carbonyl? Actually there is no carbonyl in SMILES; there is an OH and a CF3 group. Wait the SMILES: ...[C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])([F:18]) . So there is a tertiary carbon bearing OH and CF3. No carbonyl. The carbonyl-ene reaction would convert a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene to an allylic alcohol. But here we have an OH already. Maybe the retrosynthetic step is reverse: we need to break a C-O bond to form a carbonyl and an alkene. So applying template should give a carbonyl precursor (ketone) and an alkene. The template we found seems to be for converting a carbonyl-ene product to precursor (retro). The retro_smarts_template shows product side (left) is [C:1]-[CH2]-[CH2]-[C:4]-[OH] (i.e., alcohol) and reactant side (right) is [C:1]-[CH]=[CH]-[C:4]-[O]-C-aryl (i.e., carbonyl?). Actually canonical_smarts_template shows forward: [C:1]-[CH]=[CH]-[C:4]-[O]-C-aryl >> [C:1]-[CH2]-[CH2]-[C:4]-[OH]. So retro would be reverse: break C-O and form C=O and C=C. That matches.

Our molecule has a tertiary carbon with OH attached to a CF3 and part of a ring. The template expects a chain with OH attached to carbon that is attached to aromatic? Not sure.

We need to test applying each template to our molecule using apply_template tool. Let's try first template_id 672523.
